subject: Pilot credits / pricing follow-up & burn-rate check-in
messages:
From: Jordan Avery <jordan.avery@acmecorp.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-10T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot credits / pricing follow-up

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo earlier today — Jordan and Priya here from Acme. Quick recap/questions from our side: 

- Estimated monthly token volume: ~20–30M tokens (we expect spikes up to 50M during onboarding).
- Primary use: summarization + search reranking; token profile: mid-length responses (avg ~120 tokens/response).
- Budget range: targeting ~$5k–$15k/month for inference during pilot depending on unit economics.

We discussed unit economics and you mentioned a target around a certain $/1M tokens for the quantized model variants. Can you confirm a realistic $/1M tokens for our expected profile? Also, we'd like to request an extension of pilot credits if possible — current credits will run out before we finish the integration tests.

Next steps for us: get an updated estimate and confirm whether we can get an extra 50k credits to cover the onboarding spike.

Thanks,
Jordan
Jordan Avery
Senior Product Manager
Acme Corp
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Avery <jordan.avery@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-04-11T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot credits / pricing follow-up

Hi Jordan — great to meet you both today, and thanks for the clear summary. Recap + numbers below so we have an apples-to-apples comparison.

Quick unit-econ guidance (ballpark for your profile):
- Full-size variants: ~$200 per 1M tokens
- Optimized / quantized variants we typically recommend for high-volume pilots: ~$80 per 1M tokens

Estimated cost for your stated volume (example 25M tokens / month):
- Full-size: 25 * $200 = $5,000 / month
- Quantized: 25 * $80 = $2,000 / month

Both of those are within your stated $5k–$15k target depending on which variant you pick and typical traffic shape. For spikes up to 50M tokens, expectation scales linearly unless you take additional batching/caching steps (we can operate smarter there to reduce peak spend).

Pilot credits: I can request an extension. We typically approve pilot credits as dollar credits applied to the account. Based on your expected burn and to cover the onboarding spike, would an additional $2,000 in credits (roughly equivalent to 25M tokens on the quantized path) be sufficient? If so, I'll route for internal approval and confirm the cap and expiration window.

Proposed next steps:
1) Confirm which model family you want to run for the pilot (quantized vs full-size).
2) Confirm whether $2,000 in credits covers your onboarding spike — if you want more coverage we can request up to $5k but will need an internal business case.
3) I'll request the credits and share an updated pilot agreement + usage tracking link.

Would next Tuesday for a short check-in (30 minutes) work to align on model selection and sampling plan?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-04-13T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Pilot credits request — Acme Corp (requesting $2k)

Rishi — looping you in for credit approval. Summary and ask below (original thread attached).

Account: Acme Corp (deal ACME-2026-P1)
Contact: Jordan Avery, Priya Shah
Requested credits: $2,000 (to cover ~25M tokens on quantized model at $80/1M)
Timeframe: 30 days; credits to be applied to account invoice balance
Expected burn profile during onboarding:
- Week 1 (integration + smoke): ~5–10M tokens
- Week 2 (load tests + indexing): ~15–25M tokens
- Remaining pilot: ~5–10M tokens

Business case: Acme is a strategic mid-market target with potential for dedicated capacity if pilot shows 2–3x throughput and acceptable unit economics. Granting $2k covers immediate onboarding and lets the team fully validate the integration. If we want to approve a larger extension ($5k) we'll need a short revenue/commitment note from the customer.

Can you approve $2,000 in pilot credits? If yes, please confirm caps/expiration (I propose 30 days and a hard cap on credits) and whether we should create a DocuSign addendum or simply apply credits via billing.

Thanks — Marissa
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-14T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Pilot credits request — Acme Corp (requesting $2k)

Marissa — approved. Details: 
- Approve $2,000 in pilot credits for ACME-2026-P1.
- Expiration: 30 days from grant.
- Cap: credits applied on a first-come, first-serve basis; do not auto-renew.
- Billing: finance to apply credit to the account invoice; please include deal_id on the billing note.
- DocuSign: not required for this tranche; if customer requests a signed amendment, have legal prepare a short addendum and route to me.

I'll inform billing and CS to monitor usage and call out if burn rate exceeds the projected 25M tokens in 2 weeks. Reopen if customer asks for >$2k (we'll need a mini business case).

— Rishi
